[CONCLUSIONS]: Expression of a single fetal myofilament protein into adulthood in the ssTnI-transgenic mouse heart induced downregulation of the gene expression response for pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase to pressure overload. key_findings.finding: The primary experimental paper is PMID 25424393, “Metabolic efficiency promotes protection from pressure overload in hearts expressing slow skeletal troponin I” (Circulation: Heart Failure, 2015). It used adult transgenic mice expressing ssTnI/TNNI1 and nontransgenic littermates subjected to transverse aortic constriction (TAC/aortic constriction) for 12–13 weeks.

source_tools.relevance: Direct primary-paper abstract and results preview identifying model, intervention, and outcomes

key_findings.finding: ssTnI expression was associated with marked protection from pressure-overload remodeling: TAC increased heart size by about 25% in nontransgenic mice but only about 7% in ssTnI mice; echocardiographic wall thickening and diastolic LV dilation seen in controls were not significant in ssTnI hearts. Controls developed diastolic dysfunction (about 65% increase in E/A), whereas E/A decreased in ssTnI TAC hearts.

source_tools.relevance: Primary experimental paper abstract and results preview

key_findings.finding: The same study directly measured myocardial energetic and functional consequences ex vivo: isolated perfused control TAC hearts had reduced cardiac function and a 16% fall in creatine-phosphate:ATP, whereas ssTnI TAC hearts maintained cardiac function and energy charge. Thus, metabolic/energetic preservation co-occurred with protection from hypertrophy and dysfunction.

source_tools.relevance: PubTator annotations independently identifying ATP, phosphocreatine, Tnni1, and heart-failure-related entities

key_findings.finding: The evidence supports a direct mechanistic chain rather than metabolism being only a correlation: compared with control TAC, ssTnI TAC increased glucose oxidation at the expense of palmitate oxidation, prevented the TAC-associated rise in anaplerosis, and reduced PDK4 expression, enabling pyruvate dehydrogenase to compete with anaplerotic enzymes for pyruvate. The authors concluded that this improved glucose-oxidation efficiency produced energetic and functional protection against decompensation; however, the study did not independently manipulate PDK4 or substrate oxidation, so causal attribution to that metabolic pathway remains mechanistically supported but not genetically/ pharmacologically proven.

source_tools.relevance: Primary experimental paper abstract with metabolic mechanism and explicit limitation of intervention design
